_comment: Tier-2: skfem solve(K, f) without condense() on Dirichlet DoFs gives a SINGULAR stiffness matrix — solve still 'succeeds' numerically but the solution magnitude is O(1e14) or NaN. This is the canonical 'forgot to apply Dirichlet BCs' pitfall: the user wonders why their Poisson solution explodes. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 applies the documented fix at the wrong-solve site -- solve(K, f) becomes solve(*condense(K, f, D=D)) -- so K is no longer singular and the blow-up does not happen. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 3 expect_in_output strings (|u_wrong|_max = 6.434e+14); T2_MUTATE=1 gives |u_wrong|_max = 5.000e-01, the magnitude ratio drops to 1, and 'singular' disappears so the fixture goes red. Recorded while checking that: the other two expectations are not evidence of anything. 'condense' and 'magnitude' both still match under mutation because they are substrings of the fixture's own FAILURE message ('no-condense solution did NOT blow up ...; magnitude ratio < 1e6'), and forbid_in_output is empty, so 2 of the 3 expectations survive a run in which the pitfall provably no longer holds. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py CAVEAT found while adding the mutation control (assertions NOT changed): the three expect_in_output entries are prose substrings of the fixture's own English, not measured keys. With the pitfall provably removed (max|u_wrong| 6.434e+14 -> 5.000e-01) 2 of the 3 STILL match, because 'condense' is a substring of the failure message's 'no-condense' and 'magnitude' of 'magnitude ratio < 1e6'; forbid_in_output is empty, so neither FIXTURE WARNING nor Traceback is caught. Only 'singular' discriminates. Keyed assertions such as blowup_ratio_gt_1e6=True would measure this directly.
